## Explanations

### Every syllable has a tone

A tone is a pitch shape: high, rising, low or falling. It's part of the word, like its vowels. Change the tone and you get a different word.

Tap each one and listen. It's the same syllable **ma**, five times:

**mā** (mum) · **má** (hemp) · **mǎ** (horse) · **mà** (to scold) · **ma** (question word)  

### 1st tone: high and flat

Start high and hold it, like singing one note.

English: the *Aaah* at the doctor's. German: a sung *Laaa*.

The mark is a flat line: **ā**.

**mā** (mum) · **tā** · **hē** · **shī**  

### 4th tone: a sharp fall

Start high and drop fast, like a firm *No!* or *Stop!* German: *Nein!* or *Doch!*

The mark falls from left to right: **à**.

**mà** (to scold) · **tà** · **shì** · **bù**  

### High or falling?

Each pair is the same syllable, first in the 1st tone, then in the 4th. Play each pair a few times.

**mā** (mum) · **mà** (to scold)  
**tā** · **tà**  
**hē** · **hè**  
**shī** · **shì**  

### Your first sentences

Chinese word order is like English: **he / drinks**. To say *not*, put **bù** right before the verb: **he / not / drinks**.

## New words

| Pinyin | Meaning | Note |
|--------|---------|------|
| **tā**<br><sub>ta1</sub> | he / she | One word for both he and she. Only the characters are different. |
| **hē**<br><sub>he1</sub> | to drink | The h is rough, like German ch in Bach, not a soft English h. |
| **shì**<br><sub>shi4</sub> | to be (am / is / are) | Same form for I am, you are, she is. Chinese verbs never change. |
| **bù**<br><sub>bu4</sub> | not, no | Goes right before the verb: bù hē = don't drink. |
| **duì**<br><sub>dui4</sub> | right, correct | Duì! on its own means Right! / Exactly! |

## New phrases

| Pinyin | English | Literally |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| **Tā hē.**<br><sub>Ta1 he1.</sub> | He / she drinks. | he / drink |
| **Tā bù hē.**<br><sub>Ta1 bu4 he1.</sub> | He / she doesn't drink. | he / not / drink |
| **Duì, shì tā!**<br><sub>Dui4, shi4 ta1!</sub> | Right, it's him / her! | right / is / him |
